name: Vamaneeswarar Temple
deity: Shiva (Vamaneeswarar), with Parvati as Manonmani Amman
significance: A Shiva temple near Cuddalore counted among the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified in the Tevaram hymns. Its inscriptions run from Rajaraja Chola I through Rajendra Chola III, while the standing masonry temple dates to the 16th century.
story: When King Mahabali could not deliver the third pace of land he had promised the dwarf Vamana, he offered his own head instead and was granted immortality for his humility, giving the place its name.

name: Pataleeswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, this temple at Thirupathiripuliyur in Cuddalore grew through the Pallava and medieval Chola periods. It is remembered as the place where the saint Appar returned to Shaivism and later persuaded a Pallava king to abandon Jainism.
story: Appar is said to have been cured of a tormenting illness by Shiva's grace here, after which he left Jainism and devoted his life to composing hymns.

name: Netroddharakaswami Temple
significance: A Shiva temple in Viluppuram district counted among the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams. It was raised by Rajendra Chola I at the start of the 11th century and carries inscriptions from several later Chola rulers.

name: Abirameswarar Temple
deity: Shiva (Abirameswarar), with Parvati as Manonmani Amman
significance: A Shiva temple in Thiruvamaathur village, Viluppuram district, and one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams praised in the 7th-century Tevaram. The main shrine as it stands was built by Achyuta Deva Raya of Vijayanagara over older Pallava and Chola work.
story: Cows are said to have prayed to Shiva here for horns with which to defend themselves, and the place took its name from that boon.

name: Metraleeswarar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple in Kanchipuram counted among the 275 shrines praised in the 7th-century Tevaram. Its exact date of foundation is unknown, but it was enlarged in the 13th century and is maintained today by the Tamil Nadu government.
story: Shiva is said to have turned westward to listen to the hymns of the boy-saint Thirugnana Sambandar, which is how the shrine came to be called Thirumetrali.

name: Ona Kantheeswarar Temple
deity: Shiva (Ona Kantheeswarar), with Parvati as Kamakshi
significance: A Shiva temple at Panjupettai in Kanchipuram district, one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams of the 7th-century Saiva canon Tevaram. It is particularly associated with the saint-poet Sundarar, who sang of the shrine.
story: Two asuras named Onan and Kanthan are said to have found a lingam in the forest, become devotees of Shiva and built the temple, later joined by a third demon devotee, Jalandeeswaran.

name: Anekadhangavadeswarar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple in Kanchipuram revered in the 7th-century Tamil Saiva canon Tevaram and counted among the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams. It remains an active place of worship maintained by the Government of Tamil Nadu.
story: Tradition holds that Vinayaka himself installed the lingam here, and that the deity slew the demon king Kesi and brought about Vinayaka's marriage to his daughter Vallabai.

name: Sathyanatheswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, this granite Shiva temple with a three-tiered rajagopuram was already being sung about in the 7th-century Tevaram. The Archaeological Survey of India has proposed it for protection as an archaeological monument.
story: Budha, the planet Mercury, is said to have performed penance here to win a place among the nine Navagrahas after learning the shame of his birth.

name: Thirumakaraleeswarar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple in Kanchipuram district counted among the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams of the 7th-century Tevaram. The original complex is attributed to the Cholas, while the present masonry temple was raised under the Vijayanagara Nayaks.
story: Shiva is said to have appeared here as a magaral, an iguana, prompting a repentant king to build the temple after he had pursued a boy who burned a sacred jackfruit tree.

name: Talapurisvarar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple in Tiruvannamalai district celebrated in the hymns of the saint Sundarar, which makes it a Paadal Petra Sthalam. It keeps an active festival calendar including an annual Brahmotsavam.

name: Vilwanatheswarar Temple
builtDisplay: 16th c. Nayak structure; inscriptions from the 8th c.
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified in the 7th-century Tevaram, this temple in Thiruvalam preserves inscriptions running from the reign of Nandivarman II onward. Its five-tiered gopuram and unusual dvarapala figures are among its notable features.
story: Vinayaka is said to have circumambulated his parents Shiva and Parvati at this spot and won a sacred mango, so the place became Thiruvalam, meaning circumambulation.

name: Manikandeeswarar Temple, Thirumarperu
deity: Shiva (Manikandeswarar), with Parvati as Karunai Nayagi
significance: Believed to have been built by the Cholas in the 9th century with patronage from Aditya I through Rajaraja I, this is one of the 275 shrines glorified in the 7th-century Tevaram. Palaeolithic tools and megalithic remains found nearby give the site a prehistoric dimension as well.
story: Vishnu is said to have worshipped Shiva here after losing his Sudarshana discus, winning the boon that a visit to this temple counts as a visit to a thousand.

name: Jalanatheeswarar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam glorified in the Tevaram, begun under the Pallavas, enlarged by the Cholas and rebuilt in the 16th century under the Nayaks. Its 10th- and 11th-century inscriptions and its link to the Battle of Takkolam give it particular historical weight.
story: The region is said to have been swamped by floodwaters that rose to Shiva's waist, and Parvati embraced him in fear as the waters came.

name: Deivanayaka Easwarar Temple
deity: Shiva (Deivanayaka Easwarar), with the goddess Kanakakujambikai
significance: A Shiva temple in Tiruvallur district counted among the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams celebrated in the Thevaram hymns. It is remembered as the place where the saint Sambandar met Shiva and was moved to compose verses.
story: Shiva is said to have appeared to Sambandar here in the guise of an old man and commanded him to sing in his praise.

name: Tripuranthaka Swamy Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Koovam in Tiruvallur district, Tamil Nadu. It is one of the 275 sacred shrines known as the Paadal Petra Sthalams.

name: Vadaranyeswarar Temple
significance: A Chola-period Shiva temple at Thiruvalangadu and one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams. It is the Ratna Sabha or Gem Hall, one of the Pancha Sabhai where Shiva is said to have danced.
story: Karaikkal Ammaiyar is said to have approached the shrine walking on her head, thinking it a sin to tread there with her feet, and there witnessed the dance of Shiva and Parvati.

name: Vaseeswarar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple in Tiruvallur district revered in the 7th-century Saiva canon and counted among the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams. Chola inscriptions from Rajaraja I to Rajendra Chola III record grants and administrative agreements spanning centuries.
story: A cow is said to have poured milk over a mound here; when the king dug into it with a tool called a vasi blood flowed out, and Shiva later appeared to him in a dream as the snake charmer who had once saved his life.

name: Oondreswarar Temple
deity: Shiva (Oondreswarar), with Parvati as Minnoli Amman
builtDisplay: 16th c. masonry; moved to its present site in 1942
significance: A Shiva temple on the northern bank of the Poondi reservoir in Tiruvallur district, one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams of the 7th-century Tevaram and sung by the 8th-century saint Sundarar. The original Chola complex was rebuilt in the 16th century and relocated in 1942 when the reservoir was formed.
story: Sundarar is said to have lost his sight on arriving here; Shiva gave him a walking club, an oondru, which the saint threw away in disgust, breaking the horn of the temple's Nandi.

name: Adipureeswarar (Thyagaraja) Temple
deity: Shiva (Adipureeswarar / Thyagaraja), with the goddess Vadivudai Amman
builtDisplay: 11th c. Chola expansion; 7th c. Pallava origin
dynasty: Pallava, then Chola under Rajendra Chola I
significance: A major Shiva temple in northern Chennai, sung in the Tevaram and counted a Paadal Petra Sthalam, begun under the Pallavas and greatly expanded by Rajendra Chola I. It is also revered as a Shakti Pitha and once served as a centre of learning in philosophy, grammar and religious debate.
story: Sundarar, spreading the Thyagaraja cult from Tiruvarur, was tricked into vowing never to leave Tiruvottiyur and was struck blind when he broke the promise, a quarrel between the two temples still marked each year.

name: Tiruvallesvarar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple in the Padi neighbourhood of Chennai, revered in the 7th-century Tevaram and counted among the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams. Fourteen Chola inscriptions survive here, and it is one of only three temples where Guru Bhagavan is said to have worshipped.
story: Sage Bharadwaja is said to have worshipped the deity in the form of a sparrow called valiyan, which gave the temple its name.

name: Kachabeswarar Temple
significance: A twin-shrine Shiva complex at Thirukachur, one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified in the Tevaram hymns of the Nayanars. Its roots reach back to at least the 8th century, while the present masonry dates from the 16th-century Nayak period.
story: Shiva is said to have appeared here and fed the hungry saint Sundarar, an act recalled during the temple's nine-day Brahmotsavam.

name: Gnanapureeswarar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple in Tiruvadishoolam village near Chengalpattu, Tamil Nadu. It is one of the Paadal Petra Sthalams and remains a local centre of worship in the Chengalpattu district.

name: Vedagiriswarar Temple
deity: Shiva (Vedagiriswarar), with Parvati as Thiripurasundari Amman
significance: A Shiva temple at Tirukalukundram built in two parts, one on the hilltop and one at its foot, with a gopuram recalling that of Tiruvannamalai. It is one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, visited by the four great Tamil saint-poets who sang hymns there.
story: Sage Bharadwaja is said to have asked Shiva for a long life in which to master the Vedas, and Shiva raised three mountains standing for the Rig, Yajur and Sama Vedas to show him that knowledge has no end.

name: Aksheeswaraswamy Temple
deity: Shiva (Aksheeswaraswamy / Atchikontantar), with Parvati as Sundaranayagi
significance: A Shiva temple at Acharapakkam revered in the 7th-century Tamil Saiva canon Tevaram, making it a Paadal Petra Sthalam. Imitation amphorae of the 6th-7th century found at the site and inscriptions recording Chola donations give it archaeological as well as devotional value.
story: A Pandya king is said to have followed a golden iguana that vanished beneath a tree; digging there revealed a linga, and the sage Trinedhrathari built two sanctums over it.

name: Chandramouleeswarar Temple
dynasty: Chola, with patronage from Sembiyan Mahadevi
significance: A Shiva temple in Villupuram district revered in the 7th-century Tevaram and counted among the Paadal Petra Sthalams; its stone structure was raised in the reign of Aditya I. It is known for rare features including a three-faced lingam and a seven-tiered gateway tower.
story: Kali is said to have destroyed the pregnant sister of the demon Vakrasura here, and Adi Shankara later calmed her fury by installing a Srichakra at her left foot.

name: Arasaleeswarar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple in Villupuram district counted among the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams of the 7th-century Saiva canon. The original Chola shrine carries inscriptions of Vikrama Chola and Kulothunga Chola; local chieftains rebuilt the temple in the 16th century.
story: The devotion of sage Vamadeva is said to have drawn Shiva to appear beneath an arasu tree here, giving both the deity and the village their names.

name: Irumbai Mahaleswarar Temple
deity: Shiva (Maakaleswarar), with the goddess Kuyilmozhi Ammai
significance: A Shiva temple in Irumbai village, Vanur taluk of Villupuram district, close to Auroville. It is one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, glorified in the early medieval Tevaram hymns of the Nayanar Sambandar.

name: Thiruvanchikulam Mahadeva Temple
significance: The only Paadal Petra Sthalam in Kerala, this Chera-period Shiva temple at Kodungallur is revered in the 7th-century Tevaram hymns. It is remembered as the place from which the saint Sundarar and the Chera king Cheraman Perumal are believed to have ascended to Kailasa.
story: On an Adi Swathi day Sundarar is said to have risen to Kailasa on a white elephant sent by Shiva, with Cheraman Perumal following him on horseback.

name: Ketheeswaram Temple
builtDisplay: rebuilt from 1903; shrine attested for over two millennia
dynasty: Modern rebuild; earlier Pallava, Pandyan and Chola patronage
significance: One of the Pancha Ishwarams of Shiva in Sri Lanka and one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams of Tamil Saiva literature, with worship attested for well over two thousand years. Destroyed by the Portuguese in 1575, it was rebuilt by Sri Lankan Tamil devotees from 1903 onward.
story: The god of wind is said to have torn three towers from Mount Maha Meru and set one down at Thiruketheeswaram, where the Lord then established himself.

name: Gauri Kund
significance: A Hindu pilgrimage site and hot-spring bathing place in the Garhwal Himalaya at about 6,500 feet, best known as the road head and base camp for the trek to Kedarnath. It is revered as the spot where Parvati performed the austerities by which she won Shiva.
story: Parvati is said to have shaped Ganesha from the suds of her bath here, and when Shiva struck off the boy's head in anger he restored him to life with the head of an elephant.

name: Fullara (Attahas) Shakti Pitha
deity: Devi Sati, worshipped here as Phullara
significance: A temple-town in Labpur block of Birbhum district recognised as one of the 51 Shakti Pithas. It draws large numbers of pilgrims to its annual Magh Purnima fair.
story: When Mahadeva danced across the world carrying the remains of Sati, her lower lip is said to have fallen at Fullara.

name: Bahula Temple
significance: A goddess temple at Ketugram in Purba Bardhaman district counted among the 51 Shakti Pithas. It is an established pilgrimage stop for devotees of the Devi in western Bengal.

name: Bakreshwar Shakti Pitha
significance: A pilgrimage town in Birbhum district whose temple of Adi Shakti is counted among the 51 Shakta Pithas. It is one of the principal Devi pilgrimage centres of West Bengal.
story: The sage Ashtavakra, whose body had been bent in eight places by a curse, is said to have been blessed by Shiva here after many years of penance.

name: Bhabanipur Shaktipeeth
deity: Aparna (Ma Bhabani), with Vaman as the Bhairava
significance: A temple complex on the Karatoya in north-western Bangladesh counted among the Shakta Pithas of the subcontinent. It is a long-established pilgrimage centre for Hindus of the region.
story: A girl who bought conch bangles from a dealer told him to collect payment from Maharani Bhabani, and the goddess then rose from a pond wearing the bangles, revealing who the buyer had been.

name: Chandranath Temple
significance: A hilltop Shakta pitha above Sitakunda near Chittagong where Hindu tradition holds that the right arm of Sati fell. It is one of the 51 consecrated shrines linked to the myth of Sati's dismemberment and a major pilgrimage destination in Bangladesh.
story: Shiva is said to have carried Sati's body across the world in a tandava of grief until Vishnu cut it apart with his Sudarshana Chakra, sanctifying every place where a fragment came to rest.

name: Chintpurni Temple
significance: One of the five Shakta pithas of Himachal Pradesh and a major Devi pilgrimage centre in Una district, held to be the place where Sati's consciousness came to rest. The shrine also keeps Hindu genealogy registers for the families who visit it.
story: When Vishnu cut Sati's burning body into fifty-one pieces to quiet Shiva's grief, her consciousness is believed to have descended at Chintpurni.

name: Danteshwari Temple
significance: A 14th-century Kakatiya-period temple at Dantewada counted among the 52 Shakta pithas of the Indian subcontinent. It is the ritual centre of the celebrated Bastar Dussehra, which draws thousands of devotees each year.
story: A tooth of Sati is said to have fallen at this spot when her body was scattered across the subcontinent.
